title: Local base-ideal coefficient span for ideal-power sections
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], $I\subset A$ an ideal, and $J=I\mathcal O_X$ the extended ideal [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $U\subset X$ be affine and let $u_i\in F(U)$, indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$ for $r\geq0$, span $F(U)$ over $\mathcal O_X(U)$. Put $G_m=J^mF$ with its recursive power construction and image inclusion $j_m$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For every $m\geq0$, $V\subset U$, $t\in G_m(V)$ and $y\in V$, there is an open neighbourhood $W\subset V$ of $y$ such that $j_m(t|_W)$ belongs to the $\mathcal O_X(W)$-span of the sections $f^\sharp_W(a)(u_i|_W)$ for $a\in I^m$ and $i\in\operatorname{Fin}(r)$. No finite-type assumption on $F$, no finite generation of $I$, and no Rees action is assumed; only the specified affine spanning family is used.

source.place: Tag 02O8, lemma-cohomology-powers-ideal-times-F, proof, lines 5394-5398: expansion of the finite-type assertion for the ideal-power graded sheaf

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood W of y inside V. Quasi-coherence identifies F(W) with extension of scalars of F(U), so the restrictions of the u_i span F(W). This uses the affine tilde section calculation and the quasi-coherent restriction comparison; it needs no finite-type hypothesis beyond the assumed spanning family.

The extended-ideal formula identifies J(W) with the ideal generated by images of I. Induct on m in the recursive idealSheafPower construction: at zero its inclusion is the identity; at one it is J; at a successor the affine tensor/image comparison identifies the image with the product of J(W) and the preceding image. Applying the same comparison to the product with F gives image J(W)^m F(W). Ideal.map_pow identifies J(W)^m with the ideal generated by images of I^m.

Expand membership in the ideal-times-module product as a finite sum of image coefficients from I^m times elements of F(W). Express the latter in the restricted u_i and absorb their scalar coefficients into the outer O_X(W)-linear span. This is the displayed span membership. The same proof covers m=0 since I^0=A; an empty family forces F(U)=0 and hence F(W)=0.

proof_origin.note: Strict subargument of the original node: ideal-power coefficient expansion relative to given affine generators, independent of the Rees action and choice of degree-zero lifts.

theorem idealPowersLocalCoefficientSpan {A : Type v} [CommRing A]
    {X : Scheme.{v}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A))
    (I : Ideal A) (J : X.IdealSheafData)
    (hJ : J = (Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdealTop
      (I.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv.hom)).comap f)
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (U : X.Opens) (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (r : ℕ) (u : Fin r → Γ(F, U))
    (hu : Submodule.span Γ(X, U) (Set.range u) = ⊤)
    (m : ℕ) (V : X.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U)
    (t : (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι m).2 F).val.obj
      (op V)) (y : X) (hyV : y ∈ V) :
    ∃ (W : X.Opens) (hWV : W ≤ V), y ∈ W ∧
      ((Scheme.idealModuleProductι (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι m).2 F).app
        W).hom
        ((Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower J.toModulesι m).2 F).val.map
          (homOfLE hWV).op t) ∈
      Submodule.span Γ(X, W)
        {z | ∃ (i : Fin r) (a : A), a ∈ I ^ m ∧
          z = (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of A)).inv ≫
            f.appLE ⊤ W le_top).hom a) •
              F.val.map (homOfLE (hWV.trans hVU)).op (u i)}
